key_insight: A validated 4D CTA pipeline can reproducibly map patient-specific ascending aortic strain, with median strain estimates remaining robust across segmentation sources and scales.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical surrogate-mechanics tool for noninvasive assessment of aortic wall behavior that could support risk stratification and patient-specific cardiovascular planning.
method: nnU-Net or observer segmentations were remeshed into patient-specific aortic surfaces.
Deformable registration between 4D CTA phases was validated using FE-generated synthetic sequences.
Mesh-based strain was analyzed across Laplace-Beltrami spectral scales to test spatial robustness.
evidence_signal: Median strain showed minimal bias versus FE reference and narrow interobserver / model-versus-observer limits of agreement, while 95th-percentile strain was more sensitive to segmentation differences and linked to diameter, AHI, and age.
watch_item: High-percentile and regional strain measures are more segmentation-sensitive, so implementation quality and preprocessing consistency are critical for clinical use.
paper_title: Toward Reliable Patient-Specific Aortic Strain Mapping from 4D CTA: Validation, Spectral Structure, and Clinical Potential
